Interface IChromaticEffect

All Known Implementing Classes:
BreathEffect, ChromaGlitchEffect, ChromaWaveEffect, CompressEffect, ConfigurableTextEffect, CustomItalicEffect, DiscordGradientEffect, DynamicEffect, GlitchEffect, GradientEffect, LetterSpacingEffect, LiquidPlasmaEffect, MatrixRainEffect, MatrixSpinEffect, MirroredGradientEffect, PhoenixEffect, PulseEffect, RainbowWaveEffect, ScaleEffect, ShiverEffect, StaticRainbowEffect, StretchEffect, TextOutlineEffect, TimedEffect, VerticalGradientEffect, VerticalShearEffect, Volumetric3DEffect, WobbleEffect, WordFadeEffect
public interface IChromaticEffect
Describes how a piece of formatted text changes its color, position, size or outline.

The renderer samples an effect for each glyph to choose its color, position and size. The effect supplies these values; Minecraft's font renderer draws the glyph. A glyph is one drawable character shape from the font. Coordinates and offsets use GUI pixels, after Minecraft has selected its GUI scale.

FontRenderer's current draw position is called the pen position. The native renderer uses these sampling positions before applying custom transforms:

  • Per-glyph scale and offset callbacks receive the FontRenderer pen position for that glyph.
  • Color callbacks can receive the four cell corners: the pen x or x plus the native character width, and the pen y or y plus eight GUI pixels.
  • Whole-segment geometry is sampled once at the run's original x/y by TextEffectSegment.create.
For a horizontal position relative to the run, subtract getSegmentStartX() from the supplied x. getSegmentWidth() supplies the nominal run width.

Layout advance samples a per-glyph uniform scale at (0, 0). Axis-specific scales, visual offsets and whole-segment transforms leave that advance unchanged. A callback that varies scale by position can therefore draw at a different scale from the one used for its measured advance.

For a basic custom effect, implement getRenderColor, getXOffset and getYOffset. The default methods leave opacity and size unchanged and disable optional flags. Register the instance in ChromaticDefinitions under a character code or named trigger to use it in text. Add a MovementRegistry factory when callers should be able to create instances with their own palette and controls.

Implementations should read animation time from TextEffectClock.milliseconds(). The renderer freezes that clock for a draw, so different corners and background passes see one consistent animation frame. TimedEffect changes playback time independently of geometric settings such as the size multiplier or extrusion depth. For manual sampling outside a draw, open a frame scope when several callbacks must see the same moment. A direct callback does not open that shared frame by itself.

Effects are stored by reference in ChromaticDefinitions snapshots. Registration does not copy or make an implementation thread-safe. Configure a new effect before sharing it, and coordinate any later mutation yourself. Client rendering calls must return finite coordinates; ChromaticText.finite(float) rejects NaN and infinity.

  • Method Details

    • getRenderColor

      int getRenderColor(int originalColor, float x, float y)
      Chooses the color for the current glyph sample.

      The renderer can sample multiple corners to create a gradient. Return the input color when this effect should leave it unchanged. Supply transparency through getOpacity(); alpha bits in the returned color are ignored.

      Parameters:
      originalColor - color already selected by the text renderer, with RGB in the low 24 bits
      x - horizontal sample position in GUI pixels
      y - vertical sample position in GUI pixels
      Returns:
      packed RGB color; the renderer uses the low 24 bits

    • getOpacity

      default float getOpacity()
      Supplies the opacity multiplier applied to the renderer's existing alpha.
      Returns:
      finite opacity multiplier, normally zero (invisible) through one (unchanged opacity); defaults to one

    • getScale

      default float getScale(float x, float y)
      Supplies one size multiplier for both axes.

      A value other than one takes precedence over separate axis scales in the native renderer. Use one here when getScaleX(float, float) and getScaleY(float, float) should control the shape independently.

      Parameters:
      x - horizontal sample position in GUI pixels
      y - vertical sample position in GUI pixels
      Returns:
      finite uniform scale; one keeps the original size

    • getScaleX

      default float getScaleX(float x, float y)
      Supplies the horizontal scale when the uniform scale is one.
      Parameters:
      x - horizontal sample position in GUI pixels
      y - vertical sample position in GUI pixels
      Returns:
      finite horizontal multiplier; by default delegates to getScale(float, float)

    • getScaleY

      default float getScaleY(float x, float y)
      Supplies the vertical scale when the uniform scale is one.
      Parameters:
      x - horizontal sample position in GUI pixels
      y - vertical sample position in GUI pixels
      Returns:
      finite vertical multiplier; by default delegates to getScale(float, float)

    • getXOffset

      float getXOffset(float x, float y)
      Moves the glyph horizontally without changing its normal place in the text layout.
      Parameters:
      x - horizontal sample position in GUI pixels
      y - vertical sample position in GUI pixels
      Returns:
      finite horizontal displacement in GUI pixels; zero leaves it in place

    • getYOffset

      float getYOffset(float x, float y)
      Moves the glyph vertically without changing line layout.
      Parameters:
      x - horizontal sample position in GUI pixels
      y - vertical sample position in GUI pixels
      Returns:
      finite vertical displacement in GUI pixels; positive values move downward

    • isOutline

      default boolean isOutline()
      Identifies an outline effect that may decorate another primary effect.
      Returns:
      whether this effect requests an outline; false by default

    • getOutlineColor

      default int getOutlineColor()
      Chooses the outline's color separately from the foreground.
      Returns:
      packed RGB outline color; black by default

    • isVolumetric

      default boolean isVolumetric()
      Exposes the upstream volumetric capability flag.

      The 1.12 renderer obtains layer geometry from the concrete Volumetric3DEffect type. Returning true alone does not provide that geometry for an unrelated custom implementation.

      Returns:
      whether the effect advertises depth; false by default

    • isStatic

      default boolean isStatic()
      Exposes the upstream static-effect flag for API consumers.
      Returns:
      implementation-defined static classification; false by default

    • isAnimated

      default boolean isAnimated()
      Exposes an implementation's animation classification.

      The default is false even for implementations that do not override this flag but still sample time. Do not use it as a universal test that an effect never changes.

      Returns:
      the implementation's advertised animation flag; false by default

    • useHorizontalBlending

      default boolean useHorizontalBlending()
      Exposes the upstream horizontal-blending preference.
      Returns:
      whether the effect advertises horizontal color blending; false by default

    • isPassthrough

      default boolean isPassthrough()
      Exposes the upstream passthrough classification to callers.

      This flag does not automatically disable this effect's color or position callbacks.

      Returns:
      the implementation's passthrough classification; false by default

    • transformsWholeSegment

      default boolean transformsWholeSegment()
      Selects one transform for the whole consecutive run instead of a transform per letter.

      A segment is a run sharing an effect identity and its relevant outline state. Whole-segment transforms use one center and preserve the run's nominal layout width: a breathing word can grow visually without pushing the next word back and forth.

      Returns:
      true for segment-wide transformation, or false for individual glyph transforms
